items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Yeah I worked with Gus Lotz.

ctx.x: And didn't weaken. I played all the way through. You played every number from top to bottom? Every number. But no, I'd take down for the baritone a while. But I'd go back and go up again. The baritone was the only one holding it up. He'd play the lead? Yeah, baritone always played the lead. It's like the trumpet. And he used to talk about Gus Matkazzo. Boy that man could take a baritone and lead a band. Saved a lot of trumpet players. Alright, I used to talk about Gus Matkazzo. Boy that man could take a baritone…
boards? Yeah I worked with Gus Lotz. That day that there was only one trumpet, who was

your baritone player? Oh no, he was a good guy, so tall guy. He was a little bit of a trumpet player. Well this guy named Jackson, you should play tuba? Eddie Jackson. Well this guy was Kent to him, he the one who got in front of him, trumpet player. I forgot his name now, he's a much younger fella than we all was, but he played that baritone there,
